peek: Hidden tokens, a hundred in the game, that a cursed family in Kakariko pays out for.
full_text: There are a hundred Gold Skulltula tokens across the game, and the cursed family in Kakariko pays out every ten. Ten and twenty are quick and worth doing on the way past, while the full hundred is a completionist job and not something to detour for mid-playthrough.

peek: An item that shows invisible floors, walls and chests, at the cost of magic.
full_text: Equip the Lens of Truth and the invisible floors, walls and chests in the Shadow Temple all appear. It drains magic while held, so use it in bursts rather than leaving it on, and green potions and the fairies in the temple keep it running.

peek: Four bottles exist, and what you keep in them matters more than most items.
full_text: A caught fairy in a bottle revives you the moment you die, Blue Fire from the Ice Cavern melts red ice, and bugs dig up the soil patches hiding Gold Skulltulas. Never enter a dungeon with all four empty, since a fairy is the cheapest extra life in the game.

peek: Boots that sink you to the bottom of any water and hold you against wind.
full_text: The Iron Boots from the Ice Cavern sink you to the bottom of any water and hold you against wind. They are needed to reach and move around the Water Temple and to push through the gusts in the Shadow Temple, and the Zora Tunic is what lets you breathe down there.

peek: A grappling item that pulls you to wood, ladders and marked targets.
full_text: The Forest Temple gives the Hookshot, and the Water Temple upgrades it to the Longshot, which reaches twice as far. It pulls you to wood, ladders and marked targets, and drags distant chests, items and Skulltula tokens to you. When a ledge looks impossible, look for wood or a target rather than a jump.

peek: A song that stops ReDeads and Gibdos where they stand.
full_text: The Sun's Song stops a ReDead or Gibdo where it stands, leaving free hits or a clear walk past. Play it as one turns toward you, not after the scream lands.

peek: Corpses whose scream freezes you in place before they grab on.
full_text: A ReDead is a corpse whose scream freezes you in place before it grabs on and drains hearts, and the bandaged Gibdos hit hardest. Mash buttons to shake off a grab.

peek: A giant hand that drops from the ceiling and carries you back to the dungeon entrance.
full_text: The Wallmaster is slow and fragile once landed, so it only threatens you while you are standing still. Watch for the shadow spreading on the floor around you, step out of it, then kill it before it climbs back up.

peek: Powers given by the gods that last for one run.
full_text: Boons come from gods and last one run. Taking one boon from every god who offers is how runs end up with nothing that stacks.

peek: A combined boon that needs two specific gods' boons in the right slots.
full_text: A duo boon needs two specific gods' boons already in the right slots, so you cannot aim at one directly. You pick a god early, keep taking their boons, and the duo becomes possible.

peek: The permanent upgrades, bought with Darkness in your room.
full_text: The Mirror of Night holds the permanent upgrades, bought with Darkness in your room. Each row has two alternatives and you can switch between them for a small cost at any time, so nothing is locked in.

peek: A Mirror upgrade that gives free revives during a run.
full_text: Death Defiance is the Mirror of Night upgrade that changes early runs most. Each rank is another free revive mid-run.

peek: The currency that pays for Mirror of Night upgrades.
full_text: Darkness feeds the Mirror, and it is a different currency from keys and gems. Early on, keys and Darkness are both bottlenecks.

peek: A currency that unlocks new weapons and new Mirror rows.
full_text: Chthonic Keys unlock new weapons and new Mirror rows. They are a different currency from Darkness, which feeds the Mirror, and from gems, which pay for the house contractor.

peek: A currency that pays for the house contractor.
full_text: Gems pay for the house contractor. Stop taking gems once the contractor jobs you want are bought.

peek: Alternate forms of each weapon, bought with Titan Blood.
full_text: Each weapon has alternate aspects, bought with Titan Blood, that change how it plays rather than just its numbers. The last aspect for each weapon unlocks later in the story.

peek: Optional difficulty you add yourself, for rewards that only come from raising it.
full_text: Heat is optional difficulty you add yourself, in exchange for rewards that only come from raising it. It comes with the Pact of Punishment, which unlocks once you have beaten the game once.

peek: The menu that unlocks optional extra difficulty, called Heat.
full_text: The Pact of Punishment unlocks once you have beaten the game once. Heat, the optional difficulty you add yourself, comes with it.

peek: A slider that moves with how you treat people and animals.
full_text: Honor moves on small things done often, like greeting people, helping strangers on the road, paying bounties instead of running, and donating to camp. It falls for robbery, killing civilians and animals you do not use, but it is a slider, not a switch, so one bad day does not undo a good chapter.

peek: A time-slowing skill that runs on a meter you refill.
full_text: Dead Eye slows time and refills from tonics, food and clean kills. Early on it auto-marks, while later story upgrades let you paint targets yourself and eventually see weak points. Use it for the shot you cannot line up rather than for every fight, because the meter is a resource and not a mode.

peek: The reserve behind each of health, stamina and Dead Eye.
full_text: Each of health, stamina and Dead Eye has an inner core and a ring around it. The ring is the meter you spend and the core is the reserve that refills it, and the core drains from hunger, cold and injury. Eat and sleep to keep cores up, because a dead core means everything drains faster.

peek: A per-horse level that adds stamina, handling and new moves.
full_text: Bond level is what makes a horse feel different, and riding, feeding, brushing, patting and calming it during danger all raise it. Each level adds stamina, better handling, and eventually manoeuvres like the rear and the drift. Bond is per horse, so switching mounts starts again.

peek: A top-quality skin that needs a three-star animal and a clean kill.
full_text: A perfect pelt needs a three-star animal and a clean kill with the right weapon for its size. Small animals want the varmint rifle, medium ones want a bow with improved arrows, and big ones want a rifle to the head or heart.

peek: A price on your head that stays in the region where you earned it.
full_text: A bounty stays on the region it was earned in and grows with witnesses. Leave it and lawmen and bounty hunters keep coming, so pay it at any post office, and wearing a mask during a crime keeps the bounty smaller.

peek: Money put in the camp ledger that pays for camp upgrades.
full_text: The camp ledger is where camp upgrades come from: better provisions, more ammo and food to take for free, and faster fast travel from camp once bought. Contributing also keeps morale up.

peek: One rare animal per species, each in a fixed place, with its own pelt.
full_text: There is one legendary animal per species, each in a fixed place on the map, and each drops a pelt no ordinary animal gives. The Trapper is the only person who turns those pelts into clothing, and legendary animals absorb far more punishment than a normal animal of the same size.

peek: Camp-crafted upgrades that raise how much of everything you can carry.
full_text: Satchel upgrades are crafted at camp once you bring the pelts and the camp can afford it, and each tier raises how much of everything you can carry. The last one, the Legend of the East satchel, wants perfect pelts from a long list of animals.

peek: Items that refill a bar, and the gold-labelled ones also fortify the core.
full_text: Tonics refill the bar of health, stamina or Dead Eye, and the gold-labelled ones also fortify the core so it drains more slowly for a while. Carry a few tonics and a few provisions before a long ride or a fight.

peek: A score-attack mode against a clock, in one zone at a time.
full_text: Kaos is score attack against a clock in one zone at a time. You extend the time by hitting the objectives that pop up mid-riot rather than by surviving.

peek: The story mode, a chain of missions per zone.
full_text: Revolution is the story, a chain of missions per zone with objectives handed out by the resistance. It is where characters and zones unlock, and a run through it is what opens up Kaos rather than the other way round.

peek: What Kaos mode scores you on: damage, crowds and destruction.
full_text: Kaos mode scores you on chaos, and new players almost always cause too little of it. Damage, crowds and destruction are the point, not something that happens on the way to an objective.

peek: Troops who shoot from range and arrive in groups.
full_text: Corporation troops shoot from range and arrive in groups, so open ground kills you. Fight along the shopfronts and stalls where you can break line of sight, and use thrown objects and the crowd as cover.

peek: Late-round enemies with rocket launchers, the usual end of a strong run.
full_text: Late in a round, enemies start showing up with rocket launchers. They are the most dangerous thing on screen and the usual reason a strong run ends, so treat one as the priority target the moment it appears.

peek: High damage, and the easiest weapon in the game to hurt yourself with.
full_text: The rocket launcher does high damage and is the easiest weapon in the game to hurt yourself with. It is best used at range, into a crowd you are not standing in, because fired at close quarters it will take your own health down.

peek: The most forgiving heavy weapon to use on a controller.
full_text: The grenade launcher is the most forgiving of the heavy weapons to actually use on a controller. It is a good default when you want damage without fighting the aiming.

peek: Pickups around the level that each add 15 seconds to the round.
full_text: A round runs on a timer, and pickups scattered around the level add +15 seconds each. Knowing when to break off and go for time, instead of staying in a fight, is the other thing new players get wrong.

peek: A stat built at the gym or by running, cycling and swimming.
full_text: Muscle is built at a gym or by running, cycling and swimming; fourteen seconds on the treadmill or bike is one percent, and a weights rep is one percent. It raises melee damage, respect and sex appeal, but at 100% it works against sex appeal and some girlfriends will not talk to you.

peek: Endurance for sprinting, swimming and cycling.
full_text: Stamina is endurance for sprinting, swimming and cycling, and with low stamina you stop running almost immediately. It goes up with the activity itself, and finishing the Burglary side missions, ten thousand dollars of stolen goods, grants unlimited stamina regardless of the stat.

peek: A stat that goes up with food and down with exercise.
full_text: Fat goes up with food, including meals on dates, and down with exercise or with not eating. Overweight slows you down and costs health, jumping and speed, but zero fat is worse, because once there is nothing left to burn you start losing muscle and after that health.

peek: A stat that sets how many gang members you can recruit.
full_text: Respect sets how many gang members you can recruit, from one up to seven. It comes from missions, killing rival gang members and police, taking territory and spraying over tags, and it falls if you wear the wrong colours at home, kill your own, or lose turf.

peek: A level for each weapon type: Poor, then Gangster, then Hitman.
full_text: Each weapon type levels separately by hitting people and vehicles: Poor, then Gangster, then Hitman. Higher skill means better accuracy, more range, faster strafing and fire rate, and the ability to move while shooting, while thrown weapons, melee, rifles and heavy weapons have no skill meter at all.

peek: Streets you take from rival gangs, which then pay you money.
full_text: Gang territory opens up after the mission Doberman, and goes away for a stretch in the middle of the story before coming back. Holding turf pays: money accumulates and is collected outside the Johnson house on Grove Street, respect goes up, and rival gang members stop spawning in the streets you own.

peek: How long you last underwater.
full_text: Lung capacity is how long you last underwater, and it grows with time spent under. Collecting oysters is the fast way to raise it, and if the oxygen meter empties you lose health quickly.

peek: Fifty collectibles along shorelines, under bridges and in pools.
full_text: There are fifty oysters, along shorelines, under bridges and in pools, and collecting them is the fast way to raise lung capacity. All fifty, with expensive clothes and a good car, also offset the sex appeal lost to maxed muscle.

peek: Fifty collectibles around Las Venturas, all needed for 100% completion.
full_text: There are fifty horseshoes around Las Venturas, and all fifty are required for 100% completion. Each one is a hundred dollars and twenty points of luck, a stat that starts at zero and only ever goes up; the full set maxes it at 1,000.

peek: A stat that decides whether girlfriends will talk to you.
full_text: Sex appeal decides whether girlfriends will talk to you at all, and all fifty oysters covers most of that. Muscle at 100% works against it.

peek: Each protagonist's power, shown on the small yellow meter under the radar.
full_text: Each of the three protagonists has a special ability on the small yellow meter under the radar. Michael slows time in gunfights and Franklin slows time while driving. The skill behind each bar grows with use, and growing the bar grows the time you get.

peek: Michael's bullet time for shootouts.
full_text: Area Kill is Michael's bullet time for shootouts. It lasts thirty seconds once the ability bar is maxed.

peek: Franklin's power: the world slows while he is in a land vehicle.
full_text: Driving Focus slows the world while Franklin is in any land vehicle, tank included, and makes gaps and slides easy. It starts at a third of its final length, and the skill behind it climbs while he drifts, threads near misses at speed, drives into oncoming traffic, or holds ninety percent of a car's top speed.

peek: The wheel you use in free roam to switch between the three protagonists.
full_text: In free roam you can switch between the protagonists any time from the character wheel. The number under each face is how many missions that person has waiting, and you cannot switch while you have a wanted level.

peek: One of the two stock exchanges, the one that needs a Social Club connection.
full_text: The BAWSAQ is one of two stock exchanges in the single-player game, and it needs a Social Club connection. The other, the LCN, works offline.

peek: One of the two stock exchanges, the one that works offline.
full_text: The LCN is a stock exchange that works offline and reacts to what happens in the story. The other exchange, the BAWSAQ, needs a Social Club connection.

peek: The real money in the single-player game.
full_text: The real money in the single-player game is the stock market. Five assassination missions for Franklin each swing a named company, so buy that stock before the hit, wait while the market ticks every thirty seconds, and sell at the top, often eighty percent up.

peek: The shop that sells five performance upgrades per vehicle.
full_text: Los Santos Customs sells five performance categories per vehicle: engine, brakes, transmission, turbo and armour, plus cosmetic changes that do not affect handling. For a car you drive around rather than race, armour and brakes are the upgrades that pay off first, and storing the car in an owned garage is what keeps the upgrades between sessions.

peek: Dots on the map: light blue is friendly, red is hostile.
full_text: Random events appear as dots on the map: light blue is friendly, red is hostile, and flashing lets you choose a side. There are fifty-seven of them, sixty in the enhanced version, and fourteen count for completion.

peek: The shop that sells body armour in five tiers and has a shooting range.
full_text: Body armour comes in five tiers from Ammu-Nation, each a fifth stronger than the last, and once you buy a heavier one the lighter ones vanish from the shelf. Its shooting range gives three percent shooting skill per gold medal.

peek: The flashing circle on the radar where the police are looking for you.
full_text: When you are wanted, a flashing circle sits on the radar: that is where the police are looking, and every cop inside it is a flashing icon. Get outside the circle without being seen and stay quiet for a few seconds and the stars fade, but get spotted leaving and the circle re-centres on you.

peek: A garage that clears your wanted level if you enter unseen.
full_text: Pay 'n' Spray clears your wanted level if you enter it unseen in a car that fits. Any bed clears the wanted level too.

peek: Yellow street bays outside each safehouse that hold two vehicles.
full_text: There are no garages in GTA IV: the yellow Residents Parking bays on the street outside each safehouse hold two vehicles. Anything damaged there repairs itself when you leave the area or reload.

peek: Your base: walk to the bed and sleep to save.
full_text: You save by walking to the bed in a safehouse and choosing to sleep, which also clears any wanted level. The yellow Residents Parking bays on the street outside each safehouse hold your vehicles.

peek: How much a friend likes you; you raise it by taking them out.
full_text: Each friend has a like rating you raise by taking them out: bowling, darts, pool, eating, drinking, shows, the strip club. At seventy-five percent they phone to offer a favour, while being late to a date or declining their calls costs points.

peek: Side jobs picked from the computer in a stationary police car.
full_text: Sit in a stationary police car and the computer lists ten most-wanted criminals for the region. There are thirty in all across Algonquin, the Broker-Dukes-Bohan side, and Alderney, in any order you like.

peek: Two hundred hidden pigeons; getting them all spawns a helicopter.
full_text: The flying rats are two hundred pigeons hidden around Liberty City and Alderney, glowing red and cooing so you can find them at night. Shoot, burn, blow up or run over every one and the Annihilator attack helicopter spawns on the MeTV building.

peek: Fifty jumps, all needed for completion.
full_text: There are fifty stunt jumps, and unlike the pigeons all fifty are needed for completion. The game tells you after each landing: Stunt jump completed, or Not good enough.

peek: A taxi option that jumps straight to your destination for double the fare.
full_text: Once taxi rides unlock after Bull in a China Shop, you can choose the trip-skip option on the in-car terminal and the game cuts straight to arriving, at double the fare. The same terminal has a hurry option if you would rather watch the drive and get there sooner.

peek: The websites where three of the girlfriends are found.
full_text: Two girlfriends come from the story and three from the dating sites, which open after the mission Out of the Closet. Reply to a profile, wait for her email, and the first date decides whether she gives you her number.

peek: Seventeen missions that are handed out over payphones.
full_text: Seventeen of the game's missions are handed out over payphones instead of face to face. Finishing a story mission is also how new payphone jobs open up, so phones that look unavailable early on are usually just waiting on progress elsewhere.

peek: Four side courses of gates to drive through against the clock.
full_text: There are four off-road checkpoint courses. They task you with driving through a set number of gates scattered around a park, beach or car park before time runs out, purely against the clock.

peek: Four missions where you steer a toy car and smash a set number of one model.
full_text: There are four missions where you steer a remote-control car instead of walking around. Each asks you to total as many of one specific car model as you can find before time runs out.

peek: A garage that changes your car's colour and clears the wanted meter.
full_text: Driving into a Pay 'n' Spray changes your car's colour and clears the wanted meter. Finishing whatever mission you are on, or paying off a passing police bribe pickup, also clears it.

peek: A pickup that clears the wanted meter when you pay it off.
full_text: A police bribe pickup is one of the ways the wanted meter clears on its own, by paying it off as it passes. The others are driving into a Pay 'n' Spray and simply finishing whatever mission you are on.

peek: What you get when the police catch you: a fine and lost weapons.
full_text: Getting caught ends with a busted screen. Any mission in progress fails, some cash is taken as a fine, and your weapons are confiscated.

peek: Police attention on a six-star scale.
full_text: The wanted meter runs on a six-star scale. It rises from shooting, running down pedestrians, ramming police cars, or so much as aiming a gun near an officer, and a single star already brings a chase.

peek: Taxi, firefighter and paramedic work that runs apart from the story.
full_text: Vehicle-based side jobs include ferrying fares as a taxi driver, putting out fires as a firefighter, and answering emergencies as a paramedic. They run independently of the story and reward completing enough of them with a lasting bonus.

peek: A special weapon that sets off explosives you have already planted.
full_text: The detonator rounds out the special weapon category, for triggering explosives already planted. Which weapons are on hand at any moment depends entirely on what has been found or bought.

peek: A small mood effect that adds up with others into one emotion.
full_text: Moodlets add up into one emotion, and the emotion changes what your Sim can do and how fast they learn. Sad usually comes from a moodlet with a timer, such as a death, a rejection or an uncomfortable house, and it overrides better moods until it expires.

peek: The mood your Sim is in, which changes what they can do and learn.
full_text: Focused speeds up logic and programming, Inspired speeds up creative skills, and Confident unlocks bolder social options. Decorated rooms, showers, tea and thinking at a chess board are the reliable ways to choose the mood you want before starting work.

peek: A job duty to finish each day for steady income and promotions.
full_text: Complete daily tasks for steady income before expanding the house. A promotion also needs the daily task done, along with the listed skill levels, good work performance and a decent mood on the way out the door.

peek: A career step that wants skills, the daily task, performance and a good mood.
full_text: A promotion wants four things at once: the listed skill levels, the daily task done, good work performance, and a decent mood on the way out the door. The career panel lists exactly which skills and how high, and sending a Sim to work in the right emotion is usually the missing piece.

peek: The first plot of land, where a small starter home is built first.
full_text: Build a small starter home first. Career goals unlock skills, and on the Deck you should lower the sim speed in crowded lots.

peek: There are no firefighters, so keep one in the kitchen with a smoke alarm.
full_text: There are no firefighters to call in The Sims 4, so keep a fire extinguisher and a smoke alarm in the kitchen. When something catches, direct a Sim to extinguish it rather than waiting, because panicking Sims will not act on their own.

peek: A cheat that lets objects be placed anywhere, ignoring the grid.
full_text: Open the cheat console with Ctrl+Shift+C, enter testingcheats true, then bb.moveobjects on. Objects will then place anywhere, ignoring the grid and each other, and Alt while dragging frees the rotation. Things placed this way can end up unusable by Sims, so it is a decorating tool first.

peek: A text box opened with Ctrl+Shift+C for typing cheats.
full_text: Open the cheat console with Ctrl+Shift+C and enter testingcheats true. After that, one command the notes cover is bb.moveobjects on, which lets objects place anywhere.

peek: Painting and writing: money made without a career job.
full_text: Painting and writing are the classic self-employed earners because they only need one skill and one object, and both scale hard with level. Gardening is slower to start and larger later.
